source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Enter BMC Web UI -> Click "Sensor" from the menu bar.
2. Click "Sensor detail" to check each sensor. Send command: ipmitool sdr elist
3. Jam PSU FAN by a cable ties and check BMC SEL and health LED.
4. Recover and check the PSU status.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Sensor value should be OK in the reasonable range.
2. Sensor value is same as ipmi sdr command and web ui
3. BMC should record the error message and health LED shoule be amber when trigger error.
4. PSU status should recover after remove the cable ties.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Cold Reboot 25 times: perform 25 cold reboots via ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" power off; ipmitool power on. Agent loops the power-off/on 25x and logs host/BMC after each.

original_test_intent: For each fitted and applicable PSU1~N fan, create a bounded, reversible fan-stall or equivalent approved fault, verify mapped WebUI and `ipmitool sdr elist` sensor consistency, the expected BMC SEL and amber chassis-health indication, continued safe redundant power, and complete PSU/fan recovery after release.
original_method: Observe BMC WebUI sensor detail and high-level IPMI SDR, physically jam the PSU fan with a cable tie, inspect SEL and health LED, then remove the obstruction and verify PSU recovery. The cable-tie wording is preserved as source but is not executable unless the vendor explicitly approves the exact access and fixture.
manual_activity: A qualified operator identifies the exact fan and safe fixture access, applies and immediately releases the approved obstruction, observes the physical fan and amber health LED, and inspects recovery. Automation may collect synchronized read-only WebUI, IPMI, PMBus, SEL, power and host evidence.
required_inputs: Actual fitted PSU count N and per-module slot, serial, model/firmware, AC feed, fan/RPM/temperature/status SDR and WebUI identity

Vendor service or qualification document proving whether a running fan may be mechanically obstructed, the approved external fixture/access point, maximum duration and release method; no opening of an energized PSU
Per-phase Expected Values: normal baseline range, stall RPM/status and debounce, SEL assert/deassert, amber LED timing, temperature/current/load-share envelope and recovery timeout
Current PSU/feed redundancy and measured system demand, remaining-module capacity and derating margin for every tested module
Reviewed project script revision, protected BMC authentication, read-only commands, attended operator, stop/recovery owner and evidence clock
safety_requirements: Do not insert a cable tie, tool or conductive object into an energized or sealed PSU, defeat guards, open the PSU, or approach hazardous-voltage areas; use only the exact vendor-approved external fixture and trained operator procedure.
Do not replace the fan fault with 25 cold reboots, a generic power cycle or read-only baseline and claim the source coverage.
Before each module, prove the other PSU/feed group can carry measured load with margin and that the targeted PSU is not already degraded, derated or thermally abnormal.

Use independent RPM, PSU temperature, input/output current/power, load-share, redundancy and host monitoring; bound the stall duration and release immediately on limit approach, unexpected shutdown, feed loss, wrong sensor/event or fixture instability.
Export baseline SEL/logs before any approved clear; preserve the first stall event and never automatically retry or advance after an anomaly.
Test one mapped PSU fan at a time, remove the fixture completely, prove free rotation plus normal RPM/temperature/power sharing/status, SEL deassertion and full redundancy before another module.
Inspect the fan, guard and PSU for mechanical damage or retained debris; quarantine the PSU and stop if recovery is incomplete.
agent_execution_scope: Before approval, validate mapping, package, script, fixture and safety inputs without any DUT state change.
After approval, collect per-module baseline/stall/recovery WebUI and IPMI sensor values plus PMBus/power/load-share, SEL, BMC health and host continuity around the engineer action.
Compare WebUI and IPMI only for the same sensor identity, units, timestamp and update interval; report expected transient fault values separately from normal baseline/recovery ranges.
Do not touch or obstruct a fan, open a PSU, operate power, claim visual LED/fan evidence, expose credentials, clear logs, retry or issue DUT PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the fitted population, mapping, state/event matrix, fixture equivalence, load/redundancy envelope, duration, abort and recovery.
Apply/release the physical fixture, observe fan and amber LED, supervise independent monitoring and stop immediately on any limit.
Inspect hardware, verify per-module and full-system recovery and issue per-fan plus overall DUT verdicts.

modernized_recommendation.status: CONDITIONAL ON APPROVED FIXTURE AND PROJECT INPUTS
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Map every fitted PSU fan, baseline UI/IPMI/power state, apply a vendor-approved external bounded obstruction to one fan, correlate stall RPM/status/SEL/LED and redundant power, release immediately, prove full mechanical/electrical/telemetry recovery, then proceed to the next applicable fan.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact PSU model, sealed enclosure/access design, fitted population, AC-feed topology and BMC/SDR mapping.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record PSU/BMC/SDR/PMBus firmware, WebUI, ipmitool and linked script revisions plus fixture identifier.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor PSU fan-stall qualification/service, hazardous-voltage boundary, redundancy/derating, event/LED and recovery specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Retains the physical fault objective but replaces ad hoc cable-tie improvisation with an explicitly approved, non-damaging, immediately releasable fixture and adds power-path recovery evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A tach-signal or controller fault injection may cover monitoring/SEL/LED logic but does not automatically prove physical rotor stall, fan current, local heating or PSU protection; each omitted path must be recorded and cannot be called full source coverage.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: PSU/fan map, fixture or equivalent-method approval, state/event matrix, redundancy/load envelope and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A stalled internal PSU fan can create a fast local hot spot or PSU trip before BMC polling reflects it, and unsafe access can expose hazardous energy.

project_override_considerations: Project SPEC may approve a vendor fault-injection interface instead of mechanical obstruction only when it documents which physical fan, tach, thermal and PSU-protection paths are equivalent; the original cable-tie/rotor-stall method and any unverified coverage must remain visible.
expected_evidence: Preserved source/duplicate identity and approved fitted PSU1~N slot/serial/feed/fan/SDR/WebUI map
Vendor fixture/access approval, hazardous-energy boundary, duration/release SOP, operator and script/package review
Measured load, survivor/feed capacity, baseline fan RPM/temperature/current/power/load-share/redundancy, WebUI/IPMI values, SEL and health LED
Per-fan obstruction/release timestamps; matching WebUI/IPMI fault state; independent RPM/thermal/power/redundancy/host timeline; SEL assert and engineer-observed amber LED
Per-fan free rotation, normal telemetry/power sharing/status, SEL deassertion, health LED and host recovery plus physical inspection
Full redundancy restored after each module, unexpected-event review and engineer-owned per-fan/overall verdicts

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Within row 806, Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently describe a PSU-fan obstruction, BMC/UI/IPMI/SEL/LED response and recovery. The duplicate code and copied DeepSeek cold-reboot method are disambiguated prior-review/data-association defects, while `reasonable range`, N and safe fixture details are Project readiness inputs rather than contradictory core semantics.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The target and intended fault/recovery behavior are identifiable. A vendor-approved fixture, exact population, limits and operator approval can make the hybrid test ready; their absence prevents execution now but does not make the completed Review permanently blocked.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on the package/user-confirmation class while strengthening sealed-PSU energy boundaries, phase-specific sensor acceptance and load-share restoration.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: Keeps the hybrid classification but corrects source-conflict accounting and adds explicit tach-injection coverage limits and one-module-at-a-time redundancy recovery.

review_improvement: Preserves real PSU fan-fault coverage without permitting improvised access to an energized PSU, and makes every fitted fan accountable across physical stall, UI/IPMI agreement, event/LED response, redundant power and recovery.
independent_technical_reasoning: The cable action and physical LED/fan observations require a person, while mapped sensor, SEL, PMBus and recovery correlation are reasonably automatable. Because the row's purpose is clear and a vendor fixture can bound the hazard, the correct review class is package/user confirmation—not cold-reboot PARTIAL, MANUAL ONLY, or permanent BLOCKED.
